title: Making the Most Out of Growing US-Uzbekistan Trade and Investment
gist: US–Uzbekistan economic ties are deepening through purchases of U.S.-made commercial aircraft, an Uzbek company's first manufacturing facility in Kentucky, and new trade and investment frameworks; Trump has invited Mirziyoyev to the G-20 in Miami in December, and the author argues the gains must translate into Uzbek jobs and living standards.

insights.claim: Uzbekistan's purchase of U.S.-made commercial aircraft and an Uzbek company's opening of a manufacturing facility in Kentucky show growing two-way economic ties between the United States and Uzbekistan.
insights.speaker: Wilder Alejandro Sánchez
insights.so_what: Central Asian aircraft orders are a tailwind for U.S. aerospace; Uzbek outward FDI into the U.S. is a new flow to watch.
insights.locator: The purchase of U.S.-made commercial aircraft

insights.claim: U.S. diplomatic engagement with Tashkent is increasing, with new contracts and trade and investment frameworks signed.
insights.speaker: Wilder Alejandro Sánchez
insights.so_what: Framework agreements can open Uzbek critical-minerals and infrastructure opportunities to U.S. firms.
insights.locator: As U.S. diplomatic engagement with Tashkent

insights.claim: Donald Trump has invited Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev to the G-20 summit in Miami in December, where the two will next meet.
insights.speaker: Wilder Alejandro Sánchez
insights.so_what: The December G-20 is a potential venue for further US–Uzbek deal announcements.

insights.claim: Stronger US–Uzbekistan trade and investment figures must translate into employment and improved quality of life for the Uzbek population to be meaningful.
insights.speaker: Wilder Alejandro Sánchez
insights.so_what: Durability of the partnership depends on visible local benefits; watch employment-linked investment rather than headline deal values.
insights.locator: The purchase of U.S.-made commercial aircraft
